proposals.name: Unseen lens microlensing peak
proposals.idea: A previously unseen foreground object at low Galactic latitude is microlensing a red background star, causing the accelerating, roughly colour-constant rise that a Type Ia template mistook for post-peak fading. The magnification grows geometrically as the alignment improves, so the steep late rise is lensing rather than an explosion.

t_peak.meaning: time of closest lens-source alignment in days from now

u0.meaning: minimum impact parameter in Einstein-radius units

src_b.meaning: unlensed flux of the red source star in band b

base_b.meaning: unlensed blend and background flux in band b

proposals.predicts: It predicts an imminent achromatic peak near t_peak followed by a decline time-symmetric to the rise at constant colour, not the failed Ia model's already-underway asymmetric fading.

proposals.name: Close-approach inverse-square brightening
proposals.idea: A luminous or sun-reflecting body is passing the observer at nearly constant velocity with a small impact parameter, so its distance is shrinking almost linearly and its flux grows geometrically as 1/distance^2. The nearly constant, very red g-r colour and accelerating rise are therefore achromatic approach brightening, not an expanding, cooling supernova.

t_close.meaning: time in days of closest approach

tau.meaning: impact parameter divided by approach speed, in days

amp_b.meaning: peak approach flux above baseline in band b in microjansky

base_b.meaning: constant blended or background flux in band b in microjansky

proposals.predicts: It will keep brightening at constant colour to a sharp multi-thousand-microjansky peak near t_close and then decline symmetrically in time, unlike the failed SN Ia hypotheses that already have it fading and colour-evolving.

proposals.name: Magnetar delayed diffusion peak
proposals.idea: A magnetar central engine heats massive ejecta, but photons diffuse out slowly so the transient is still on its steep rising branch about a month after explosion. The faint early flux is host light plus the first diffusing emission, not a normal Type Ia maximum.

t_exp.meaning: explosion time in days relative to now

t_diff.meaning: diffusion time from explosion to bolometric peak

amp_b.meaning: peak source flux in this band

host_b.meaning: constant host and precursor flux in this band

proposals.predicts: It predicts continued brightening for weeks to a broad luminous maximum near t_exp+t_diff followed by a slow decline, rather than the immediate post-peak fade of the failed Ia model.
